subject: Action: Data ownership and DPA clarifications (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Long <sara.long@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-08-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Action: Data ownership and DPA clarifications (Acme Health)

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of the call
- Acme will act as the Controller; Redwood would be the Processor for inference requests (confirmed by Sara on the call).
- Use cases: clinical triage assistant (low-latency inference from EHR extracts) and patient messaging summarization.
- Primary concerns raised: data residency, retention of logs/responses, subprocessor visibility, and breach-notification timing.

Open items / questions from Redwood:
1) Residency: confirm whether all production data must remain in US-only, or if EU processing is acceptable for EU patient subsets.
2) Retention: what is the required retention period for request/response pairs and for audit logs? You mentioned "long-term archives for compliance" — can you specify years?
3) PII handling: will Acme pre-redact PHI before sending or expect Redwood to provide additional redaction/pseudonymization?
4) Subprocessors: procurement asked for a notice window; please confirm your expectation (30 days, 14 days, immediate notice).
5) Breach notification SLA: what is Acme's required notification window for vendor-detected incidents?

Proposed next steps
- Ben and Rishi to respond today with technical & DPA language suggestions (logging, retention, KMS/HSM details).
- I'll attach our demo notes and a baseline DPA redline for your review (we will circulate redline by EOD).
- If it helps, let's schedule a 30-minute legal/technical call early next week to run through the redline.

Attachments: acme-demo-notes-20270811.txt (demo notes)

Thanks — looking forward to tightening up the DPA language and confirming the rollout constraints.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Sara Long <sara.long@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action: Data ownership and DPA clarifications (Acme Health)

Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from Acme's side: 

- Confirmed: Acme is Controller for patient data and Redwood will be Processor.
- Residency: Production patient data must remain in US-only. EU processing is not acceptable for US patients; for EU patients we can discuss EU-residency later.
- Retention: procurement/legal are asking for retention limits in the DPA — target is 2 years for logs and request metadata, and we need an archive option for 7 years on a per-request basis for legal holds.
- Subprocessors: Procurement requests a 30-day notice before adding a new subprocessor and the ability to object.
- Breach notifications: Acme requires vendor-detected incidents to be reported within 24 hours of detection.

We'll also need a current list of subprocessors and SOC2 Type II evidence. Procurement will review your redline and loop in our legal team.

Can you provide:
1) A CSV with your current subprocessor list
2) A proposed clause for breach timing and breach-handling playbook
3) DocuSign-ready DPA redline

Thanks,
Sara Long
Head of Partnerships, Acme Health
sara.long@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Long <sara.long@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-08-11T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action: Data ownership and DPA clarifications (Acme Health)

Sara — quick technical notes to address the retention / logging and residency questions: 

- Residency: Hosted Redwood API is region-aware; we can pin Acme's workload to US regions only for production. For strict physical separation we can option you into Dedicated or Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed keys.

- Request/response retention: default is 30 days for full request+response payloads in hosted mode. We retain request metadata/audit logs for 90 days. We can extend both values via contractual configuration up to your requested 2 years for metadata and archival pathways for longer retention, but longer retention increases exposure scope and cost.

- Caching/KV: inference KV cache is memory-backed and evicted per policy; we do not persist KV cache to disk in hosted mode. We can enable automatic redaction rules at the prompt and response layer (pattern-based or via an allowlist of fields).

- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor CSV. We provide weekly updates internally and can commit to a 30-day notice window (subject to our standard exceptions for security fixes).

Attachments: subprocessor-list-20270811.csv

If helpful I can join the legal call to walk through the technical ramifications of retention windows and to explain costs and fallback options (e.g., pseudo/anonymization on ingest).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Long <sara.long@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-08-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action: Data ownership and DPA clarifications (Acme Health)

Sara / team — looping in proposed contract language and our privacy position. Below is a concise starter for the DPA section you asked about; I'll attach a redline for your review.

Suggested DPA snippets (starter):
- Roles: "Acme Health shall be the Controller and Redwood Inference shall be the Processor with respect to Personal Data processed under this Agreement."
- Subprocessors: "Processor may engage Subprocessors. Processor will provide Controller with at least thirty (30) days' prior notice of the addition of any Subprocessor and will provide a current list of Subprocessors upon request. Controller may object to a new Subprocessor within fifteen (15) days on reasonable grounds relating to data protection; if objection is not resolved, parties will work in good faith to find an alternative."
- Breach notification: "Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay and, where feasible, within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of a Security Incident affecting Controller Data; Processor will provide timely updates as information becomes available. The parties acknowledge that Controller may require a shorter notification window; such requirements must be agreed in writing in the Order Form."
- Retention: "Processor will retain Request Metadata for a period configurable up to two (2) years and Request/Response payloads for a standard period of thirty (30) days unless otherwise agreed in writing. Processor will provide an archival mechanism to retain data for up to seven (7) years for compliance/legal-hold requests at Controller's expense."

Notes:
- We typically propose 48 hours for vendor-detected incidents as a reasonable operational SLA; 24 hours is aggressive but we can commit to escalations and will document a runbook for high-priority incidents (we can also offer dedicated PagerDuty routing for Acme if needed).
- We will provide SOC 2 Type II report and can provide the redlined DPA via DocuSign.

I've attached the redline: redlined-dpa-acmehealth-20270811.pdf and the current subprocessor list (CSV). I can join your procurement/legal call to walk through clauses.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
